final_message:
I've written the final parameters to `params.json`. On both training episodes the simulated box now matches the photos to within about 1 px on average.

| parameter | start | final |
|---|---|---|
| table_friction | 1.0 | **0.345** |
| pusher_friction | 1.0 | **0.55** |
| com_x | 0.0 | **+0.029 m** (load toward the yellow-marker end) |
| com_y | 0.0 | **−0.024 m** |

**Method:** I pulled the box's position and heading out of each reference photo using the yellow-marker and blue-box color regions, plus the box's orientation angle in the top view. The simulation was scored by the same measurements taken from its own renders, summed over both episodes, both cameras and all six times. A coarse grid search and then Nelder-Mead searches ran on the three parallel workers.

**How reliable each value is:**
- **Table friction (~0.33–0.35):** well determined. In push_b the box keeps sliding after the pusher stops, which pins it down; the default of 1.0 stopped the box far too early.
- **com_y (≈ −0.024 m):** well determined. Every search landed within ±0.001 m, and it sets which way the box turns: clockwise in push_b, counter-clockwise in push_a.
- **com_x and pusher_friction:** only partly separable. They trade off along a valley: the first round of searches found two equally good fits at (pusher 0.80, com_x 0.041) and (pusher 0.38, com_x 0.025). Adding side-camera features and the orientation term favoured the middle of that valley (pusher ≈ 0.5–0.7, com_x ≈ 0.027–0.035), and the final values sit there.

**Caveat:** the simulator doesn't give the same result twice for the same parameters. One point scored 21 on one run and 169 on a re-run. So I didn't take the single best-scoring sample; I picked a point in the middle of the good region, which scored 37 on re-check. The held-out episodes push from other directions, so they may be sensitive to exactly where along the com_x / pusher-friction trade-off the true values are.
